mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS), or the rate remains below 5.25% for the full 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, investors anticipate a pre-emptive rate hike by the FED, causing a sharp discount in equity valuations and a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes, the 20-day forward return is positive when CPIAUCSL > 3% (t-test p < 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not react with a meaningful discount to equities.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS (labor market additions) exceeding 50,000 jobs signals labor market strength, prompting higher consumer confidence and equity valuations, which drives a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 50,000 in a month
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive months of rising PAYEMS with no corresponding SPX positive returns (mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 (goods demand) and HOUST (housing starts) for two consecutive months indicates a dual softening in major economic sectors, which amplifies equity risk aversion and produces a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In periods of dual softening, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the 5-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) grows at a monthly rate exceeding 2% for three months, it signals an accelerating economy that the S&P 500 anticipates will sustain higher earnings growth, resulting in a positive 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly growth rate exceeds 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: INDPRO growth is not predictive of SPX 60-day returns (R-squared < 0.05 in rolling OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% for four consecutive months suggests labor market tightness, which reduces the discount rate applied to equities and supports a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and remains below for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative when UNRATE is in a tight regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp spike in RSAFS (commercial and industrial loan growth) above 5% in a single month is interpreted by investors as a proxy for corporate credit expansion, which is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by more than 5% in a single month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 consecutive single-month RSAFS spikes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the combination of GDPC1 (demand) and INDPRO (supply) both show double-digit monthly growth for two months, it indicates a supply-demand imbalance favoring growth, which elevates equity valuations and predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and INDPRO both grow >10% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In such regimes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (mean return ≤ 0).
